title: Apple Data Protection Class Hierarchy & KDF Specification

classes.name: Class A (Complete Protection)
classes.locking_behavior: Keys discarded immediately from memory upon device lock (secret_drop). Inaccessible until user passcode entry.
classes.intended_usage: User sensitive data: Health data, Mail messages, Safari history, Photos, Keychain items.
classes.key_recovery: Passcode required. Key derivation fails immediately if device is locked.

classes.name: Class B (Protected Unless Open)
classes.locking_behavior: Keys retained in memory for currently open files even when the device locks. New files can be created while locked via asymmetric curve derivation.
classes.intended_usage: Background downloads, Mail attachments being downloaded in background, audio recordings.
classes.key_recovery: Public key encrypts new file key; private key required to decrypt and open existing files.

classes.name: Class C (Protected Until First Unlock)
classes.locking_behavior: Keys decrypted upon first user passcode entry post-boot and retained in memory across subsequent lock/unlock cycles until reboot.
classes.intended_usage: Background system daemons, push notification delivery, alarm clock, calendar reminders.
classes.key_recovery: Accessible across lock states as long as the device has booted and been unlocked at least once.

classes.name: Class D (No Protection / Effaceable)
classes.locking_behavior: Encrypted using D-Key stored in Effaceable Storage. Always accessible regardless of lock state.
classes.intended_usage: System binaries, caches, non-sensitive assets. Wiped instantly upon Erase All Content and Settings.
classes.key_recovery: Hardware key in Effaceable Storage wiped instantly to achieve cryptographic erase.

passcode_iteration_kdf.hardware_binding: scrypt output is hashed with UID0 using hardware AES-CMAC

file_key_wrapping.role: Wraps individual per-inode file encryption keys under class protection keys.
